quiz.question: Which technique prevents infinite loops in user-submitted code?
options: Load balancers distributing requests across multiple worker instances
quiz.explanation: A hard execution time limit kills runaway code so it can't monopolise a worker.

quiz.question: Why is running user code directly on the API server a bad idea?
options: It is too slow to start
Malicious code could compromise the server and other users' data
quiz.explanation: Untrusted code needs isolation. On the API server it can read files, exhaust resources, or attack the host.

quiz.question: What data structure makes a real-time competition leaderboard cheap to maintain?
options: A B-tree index on every column
quiz.explanation: Sorted sets keep members ordered by score, so updates and top-N reads are O(log n).

quiz.question: What does adding a queue between the API server and code-execution containers buy you?
options: Buffering submissions during spikes so none are dropped
Lower per-submission latency in every case
quiz.explanation: The queue absorbs bursts (e.g. at the start of a contest) while workers scale out and drain it.
